baseline_facts.content: Patient's full name is Jack Armani.
Patient's date of birth is twelve August nineteen fifty eight.
Patient is unable to move the left arm.
Left arm immobility started about an hour before the call.
Patient reports no pain in the left arm.
No discoloration is present in the hand.
The hand does not feel cold.
Patient reports tingling on the left side of the face.
Tingling on the left side of the face began about an hour before the call.
Patient reports difficulty swallowing.
Patient reports speech is slower than normal.
Patient needs to think more before speaking.
Patient did not notice facial asymmetry.
Patient has no symptoms in the left leg.
At the time of the call, the left arm still cannot move.
At the time of the call, speech is getting more difficult.
Patient reports no previous episodes of left arm immobility.
No unusual sleeping position last night.
No one else is at home at the time of the call.
Patient normally lives alone.
Patient has type two diabetes.
Patient has high blood pressure.
Patient takes Metformin.
Patient takes losartan.
Patient takes Amlodipine.
Patient is allergic to penicillin.
Patient's father has heart disease.
Patient used to smoke.
Patient drinks a few alcoholic drinks over the weekend.
Patient drinks a couple more alcoholic drinks during the week.
Patient drinks beer in pints.
Doctor suspected the symptoms may be due to a stroke.
An ambulance was called to the patient's home address.

candidate_facts.content: Symptom onset occurred approximately 1 hour prior to the call.
Symptoms began upon awakening.
Patient awoke with complete inability to move the left arm.
Patient reported no pain in the left arm.
Patient reported tingling on the left side of the face.
Patient reported difficulty swallowing.
Patient reported that speech felt slower and more effortful.
Patient did not notice any facial asymmetry.
Patient reported no symptoms in the left leg.
Patient reported no discoloration of the hand.
Patient reported the hand did not feel cold.
Patient slept as usual prior to symptom onset.
Patient reported no awkward positioning during sleep.
No prior episodes of similar symptoms were reported.
Symptoms persisted during the call.
Patient reported possible worsening of symptoms during the call.
Past medical history includes type 2 diabetes mellitus.
Past medical history includes hypertension.
Patient takes metformin.
Metformin indication is type 2 diabetes mellitus.
Patient takes losartan.
Losartan indication is hypertension.
Patient takes amlodipine.
Amlodipine indication is hypertension.
Patient has a penicillin allergy.
Family history includes father with heart disease.
Patient lives alone.
Patient is a former smoker.
Patient drinks beers (pints): a few over the weekend and a couple during the week.
Vital signs were not obtained.
Physical examination was not performed due to telephone consult.
No laboratory results were available.
No imaging studies were available.
No procedures were performed.
Clinician assessed the presentation as highly concerning for acute cerebrovascular event (stroke).
Differential diagnosis included ischemic stroke as most likely.
Differential diagnosis included intracerebral hemorrhage.
Peripheral nerve or plexus lesion was considered unlikely.
Emergency medical services were activated during the call.
Patient was to be transported to the emergency department by ambulance.
Patient was instructed to unlock the front door.
Patient was instructed to sit in the hallway near the entrance.
Clinician remained on the phone until EMS arrival.
Stroke team evaluation was planned in the emergency department.
Patient was informed of concern for stroke.
Patient was advised of the need for immediate hospital-based assessment and possible treatment.
Remote monitoring was performed during the call.
Patient was advised to avoid oral intake.
Patient was advised to await EMS.
No changes to diabetes management were made during the call.
No changes to hypertension management were made during the call.
Follow-up was to be determined after emergency department evaluation.
